nodes.summary: The classic skyline estimate `θ̂_k = C(k, 2) w_k` for the interval with `k` lineages.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of the skyline maximizer

nodes.summary: The skyline estimate maximizes the interval likelihood (Pybus, Rambaut & Harvey 2000): for `c, w, θ > 0`, `ℓ(θ) ≤ ℓ(c w)`.
nodes.title: The skyline estimate maximizes the interval likelihood

nodes.summary: The log-likelihood of `θ` for one coalescent interval of length `w` with `c = C(k, 2)` pairs of lineages: the log-density `log (c / θ) - c w / θ` of `Exp(c / θ)` at `w`.
nodes.title: Log-likelihood of one coalescent interval in the skyline model

nodes.summary: The canonical probability space for the skyline model: the product of the exponential laws `Exp(C(k, 2) / θ k)`, `2 ≤ k ≤ n`.
nodes.title: Canonical probability space for the skyline model

nodes.summary: The coalescent intervals of a sample of `n` genes under the classic skyline model with piecewise-constant population-size parameter `θ k` while there are `k` lineages: `T k` is exponential with rate `C(k, 2) / θ k`, independently over `2 ≤ k ≤ n`.
nodes.title: Coalescent intervals under the classic skyline model

nodes.summary: Equality in `sum_skylineLogLik_le` holds iff `θ i = c i w i` for every interval.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the joint maximizer

nodes.summary: For positive `c i`, `w i`, `θ i` over a finite set of intervals, `∑ ℓ_i(θ_i) ≤ ∑ ℓ_i(c_i w_i)`.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved

stated.label: statement formalized
